claim: Code differs from natural language for uncertainty estimation purposes in three ways: token fragility (one wrong token breaks the whole program), the intent-code gap (algorithmic intent and implementation can diverge independently), and executability.
stance_target: motivates code-native (not NL-ported) uncertainty/confidence methods -- same motivating premise as the proposed AAAI headline
quoted_support: We argue that code differs from NL in three ways: a single wrong token can break an entire program (token fragility); algorithmic intent and concrete implementation can disagree independently (intent-code gap); and programs can be executed (executability).

claim: An ensemble of three orthogonal uncertainty axes (lexical token entropy, algorithmic pseudo-code consistency, functional behavioral consistency) improves average AUROC from 0.696 for the strongest NL-derived baseline to 0.776 across five code LLMs.
stance_target: state-of-the-art code UE discrimination performance as of mid-2026
scope_conditions: five code LLMs, inference-time ensemble UE
quoted_support: our three-axis ensemble improves average AUROC from 0.696 for the strongest NL-derived baseline to 0.776 (+8.1 points).

claim: Single-pass Top-K token entropy on Qwen3-14B matches the strongest multi-pass sampling-based UE baseline while being over 3x cheaper computationally.
stance_target: cost-efficiency of lexical UE signals vs sampling-based confidence
quoted_support: on Qwen3-14B, our single-pass Top-K token entropy matches the strongest multi-pass baseline while being over 3x cheaper.

claim: This method produces a single scalar per-problem/per-generation uncertainty score via an inference-time ensemble, not a per-test-case dense confidence output, and involves no training of the code LLM to self-express confidence.
stance_target: PARTIAL occupancy: shares code-native UE motivation but distinct mechanism (inference-time ensemble vs trained per-test dense expressed confidence)
scope_conditions: code UE evaluated via AUROC discrimination
quoted_support: These results suggest that code UE deserves code-specific design rather than direct NL ports.
